name: Primary school with class teachers
summary: One teacher takes their class for most of the week, with a few specialists who move between classes for music, sport and art.
when_to_choose: Choose this if each class has its own teacher who covers most subjects, and the timetable's real job is to fit the specialists and the shared spaces around them.

knobs.label: Days in the timetable cycle
knobs.help: Five for a timetable that repeats every week. Ten if the specialists work to a two-week pattern.

knobs.label: Periods in a school day
knobs.help: Count the blocks the day is divided into, not the hours. Many primary schools work in six or seven.

knobs.label: Length of one period
knobs.help: In minutes. Longer blocks suit younger classes; the specialists' lessons are usually one or two of these.

knobs.label: Main break comes after this many periods
knobs.help: The break everyone shares. Three means the break falls after the third period of the morning.

knobs.label: Subjects taught by a specialist
knobs.help: How many subjects are taken by someone other than the class teacher - typically music, physical education and art.

questions: How many classes are there in each year group?
Which subjects are taken by a specialist rather than the class teacher?
Do the specialists work every day, or only on certain days?
Which spaces are shared - a hall, a field, a music room - and how many classes can use them at once?
Do any classes need to be free at the same time, for assembly or shared reading?
tradeoffs: Giving each class teacher a long unbroken block for literacy and numeracy protects the morning, but it pushes every specialist lesson into the afternoon, where the hall and the field then run short.
A part-time specialist who works two days makes the rest of the week simpler but forces several classes to take the same subject on the same two days.
A two-week cycle lets a specialist see each class fortnightly rather than squeezing everyone into one week, at the cost of parents and children having to remember which week it is.
